<div class="note">
<span class="lab">What you will end up with</span>
<p>Synthetic cohorts whose marginals, missingness, correlation structure and design cells are those
of real data, carrying programmes chosen in advance, and a score for how much of that planted truth
the estimator gave back.</p>
</div>

## What a simulation has to reproduce, and what it does not

The estimator reads a normalised feature-by-sample matrix. Fragment bias, retention time,
ionisation efficiency and isotope envelopes are modelled upstream of that matrix, and normalisation
removes or absorbs them before anything reaches the estimator. The simulation target is therefore
not measurement physics but the six properties of a prepared matrix the estimator can respond to:

1. the per-feature marginal distribution, including its skewness and tail weight;
2. the mean-variance relation across features;
3. missingness as a function of abundance;
4. the feature-feature correlation structure, summarised by its eigenspectrum;
5. the non-Gaussianity the identification argument rests on;
6. the design margins, including unpopulated cells and covariates recorded in only one cohort.

A generator that reproduces these six reproduces everything the estimator can respond to. This is
what lets the package borrow realism from data rather than assert it through a distributional
choice, and it is why no count model or mass-spectrometry error model appears anywhere below.

## Three tiers, and what each establishes

| Tier | What is simulated | What it establishes |
|---|---|---|
| Parametric | Non-Gaussian, pairwise-different, non-symmetric sources; Gaussian loadings with planted pure features | The estimator is correct when its own assumptions hold |
| Borrowed marginals | The same latent structure, read through the marginals, missingness, correlation and design cells of real layers | How recovery changes when the matrix has the shape of the data the method is applied to |
| Planted pathways | Shared programmes that are curated pathways, in the features that belong to them | Whether the biological channel recovers biology it was not shown |

The first tier needs nothing but `chorale_simulate()`. The second and third are built on a shape
profile.

## Tier one: the parametric simulator

`chorale_simulate()` plants latent sources that satisfy the identification conditions by
construction. Every source is non-Gaussian, no two share a distribution, and each is non-symmetric.
A shared factor carries a **design signature**, one weight per design contrast, which is the same in
every modality; its remaining variation is drawn independently per modality, because the samples are
disjoint. Matching modalities on their design response is therefore what the truth rewards.

```r
library(chorale)

sim <- chorale_simulate(
  n_modalities      = 3,
  n_features        = 400,
  n_shared_factors  = 2,
  n_private_factors = 1,
  effect_size       = 3,
  seed              = 1
)

containers <- Map(chorale_load, sim$modalities, sim$col_data)
fit <- chorale_fit(containers, n_factors = 3, n_init = 5)
chorale_score_recovery(fit, sim)
```

`chorale_score_recovery()` reduces the fit to the quantities a validation cares about: how many
programmes were supported, how many of them correspond to one planted shared factor, the accuracy of
the assignments, and the share of planted shared factors recovered as a programme spanning at least
two modalities.

`chorale_validate()` runs a grid of regimes and averages those metrics over replicates. Setting
`effect_size = 0` detaches the shared factors from the design and gives the complete null;
`same_response = TRUE` plants two shared factors with the same phenotype response, which is the
adversarial case the design channel cannot separate and should not merge.

```r
grid <- data.frame(
  label         = c("clean", "weak", "null", "same_response"),
  effect_size   = c(3, 1, 0, 3),
  same_response = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE)
)
chorale_validate(grid, n_rep = 5)
```

## Tier two: giving the simulation the shape of real data

`chorale_data_profile()` measures the six properties from any matrix and returns them as one object.
It stores summaries rather than data: no sample identifier enters it, and no covariate you withhold.
Name the design columns you want profiled, and identifying fields stay out.

```r
profile <- chorale_data_profile(
  assay      = my_matrix,
  col_data   = my_design,
  covariates = c("phenotype", "sex"),
  layer      = "PROT"
)
profile
```

The covariates you profile are the terms a planted signature can be written over, since a signature
means the same thing in every modality only where every modality carries the term.
`chorale_signature_terms()` reports them.

Passing the profile to `chorale_simulate()` leaves the latent structure untouched and replaces the
observation model with it. Each simulated feature is read through a real feature's quantile grid, so
the values that come out have the distribution a real feature had, and the map is monotone, so the
sign and the ordering of a planted design response survive it. The design is drawn from the cells
the real cohort populated, so a cell no sample occupied stays empty.

```r
sim <- chorale_simulate(
  n_modalities      = 3,
  n_features        = 400,
  n_shared_factors  = 2,
  n_private_factors = 1,
  effect_size       = 3,
  profile           = list(profile_rna, profile_prot, profile_metab),
  seed              = 1
)
```

Marginals are imposed feature by feature and therefore carry nothing about how features covary.
Correlation enters separately, as directions drawn at random in feature space with Gaussian scores
whose variances follow the profile's eigenvalues, scaled until the leading direction of the
simulated matrix carries the share of the variance the profile records. Their scores are Gaussian,
so they add covariance without adding anything a component analysis driven by non-Gaussianity could
recover as a source. Set `background = FALSE` to leave them out.

`chorale_profile_agreement()` places a simulated matrix beside the real one on the same six
properties, which is what a claim of realism is bounded to.

```r
chorale_profile_agreement(chorale_data_profile(sim$modalities[[1]]), profile_rna)
```

<div class="note">
<span class="lab">The factor count is not a detail</span>
<p>A matrix carrying the correlation structure of real data supports more components than were
planted. On the reference layers, fixing the count at the number planted recovers 0.30 of the
planted programmes where taking it from the detectability gate recovers 0.70. Under the parametric
observation model both settings recover all of them, so that tier cannot see this. Pass
<code>n_factors = "auto"</code>, or an <code>n_factors</code> column in a
<code>chorale_validate()</code> grid.</p>
</div>

## Tier three: planting curated pathways

`chorale_plant()` makes the shared programmes curated pathways rather than anonymous factors. Each
planted programme occupies the features that belong to one set in every modality that can express
it: the genes of the set in a transcriptome or proteome, and the lipid classes the same set acts on
in a lipidome. Recovery can then be scored on biology, which no real cohort supports, since no real
cohort records which features belong to a programme.

**The vocabulary a programme is planted from is not the vocabulary it is scored in.** Planting from
the collection the pathway channel regresses on would make that channel succeed by construction. A
planting set is admitted only where its overlap with every scoring set falls below `max_jaccard`,
and the realised overlap travels with the result. `chorale_set_overlap()` reports it directly.

```r
plant_sets <- chorale_genesets("kegg", db_species = "HS")
score_sets <- chorale_genesets("reactome", db_species = "MM")

membership <- list(
  RNA   = chorale_geneset_matrix(entrez_rna,  plant_sets, min_features = 1),
  PROT  = chorale_geneset_matrix(entrez_prot, plant_sets, min_features = 1),
  METAB = chorale_metabolite_matrix(lipid_ids, plant_sets,
                                    mapping = my_lipid_class_table,
                                    min_features = 1)
)

planted <- chorale_plant(
  profiles        = profiles,
  membership      = membership,
  plant_sets      = plant_sets,
  score_sets      = score_sets,
  n_programmes    = 3,
  member_fraction = 0.6,
  leak_fraction   = 0.2,
  max_jaccard     = 0.4,
  seed            = 1
)
planted$plant
```

KEGG is distributed in MSigDB as a human collection and reaches other organisms through orthologs,
so it is registered under `HS` alone; asking for it mouse-native is refused by name. Reactome is
registered under both.

Two dials govern how far a planted signal departs from a clean set indicator. `member_fraction` is
the share of a set's features that carry the programme, and `leak_fraction` is the share of the
programme's loading mass placed on features outside the set. The planted truth is recorded as the
features that actually received loading, so identifier mapping losses are absorbed rather than
assumed away.

Fit the planted data with the **scoring** collection, then score it.

```r
containers <- Map(chorale_load, planted$sim$modalities, planted$sim$col_data)
fit <- chorale_fit(containers, n_factors = 10, gene_sets = score_sets,
                   feature_map = feature_map, feature_space = c(METAB = "lipid"),
                   n_init = 10)

scored <- chorale_score_planting(fit, planted, score_sets, overlap = 0.1)
scored$per_modality
scored$channel
```

`chorale_score_planting()` reports three quantities, one per question the planting was built to
answer.

- **Pathway ranking** (`pathway_auc`): the probability that a scoring set overlapping the planted
  pathway outranks one that does not, in the recovered composition. Chance is 0.5.
- **Marker precision**: the share of the pure features a factor reports that fall inside the planted
  set.
- **Channel specificity** (`channel`): whether the pathway channel reaches significance for planted
  programmes and stays quiet elsewhere.

## What the reference runs found

Three pathways planted at the production depths of a transcriptome, a proteome and a lipidome.
Glycerophospholipid metabolism and fatty acid metabolism reached all three layers; pathways in
cancer reached the first two and not the lipidome, which makes its lipidome entry a control.

| Programme | RNA | PROT | METAB |
|---|---|---|---|
| Glycerophospholipid metabolism | 0.53 | 0.84 | 0.55 |
| Fatty acid metabolism | 0.29 | 0.93 | 0.69 |
| Pathways in cancer | 0.80 | 0.94 | 0.26, not planted |

Recovery tracks how many members of a pathway a modality carries. The proteome carried between 33
and 162 and recovered all three at 0.84 to 0.94. The transcriptome was reduced to its 2,000 most
variable genes upstream, carried between 5 and 42, and recovered them from 0.29 to 0.80. The
lipidome reaches a pathway through its classes, at 0.55 and 0.69, and the pathway never planted
there sits at 0.26.

Under a genuine null the joint p-value is conservative rather than uniform: across thirty null
datasets drawn from real profiles, twenty-eight exceeded 0.5 and the false positive rate at the
nominal five per cent was 0.033.

## Conditions of applicability

Recovery measured under borrowed marginals holds for marginals resembling the profiled ones. A
modality whose distribution or missingness differs materially requires its own profile.

A pathway reaches a modality only through the identifiers or classes that modality carries. A
lipidome resolves at the level of lipid class, not lipid species, and a metabolome with no class
mapping cannot be planted.

The Jaccard ceiling separating the planting and scoring vocabularies is a threshold rather than a
property of the biology. A pathway planted from a set with a near-identical counterpart in the
scoring collection would be recovered by construction, which the ceiling excludes and the reported
value documents.

Correlation outside the planted programmes is reproduced as its eigenspectrum, through directions
drawn at random in feature space. Those directions carry no biological grouping, so a modality whose
dominant axis has a biological identity is reproduced in the share of variance that axis carries and
not in which features it uses.

Pure features are rare once the covariance is realistic, so the marker precision is informative for
the few factors that carry any rather than for all of them.
